definitions.explanation: a concise summary of an academic paper, article, or document highlighting key points

examples.japanese: {論文|ろんぶん}の{抄録|しょうろく}を{読|よ}んだ。
examples.english: I read the abstract of the paper.

examples.japanese: {抄録|しょうろく}は200{語|ご}{以内|いない}で{書|か}いてください。
examples.english: Please write the abstract in 200 words or less.

examples.japanese: {学会|がっかい}{発表|はっぴょう}の{抄録|しょうろく}を{提出|ていしゅつ}した。
examples.english: I submitted the abstract for my conference presentation.

notes:
FORMATION:
{抄|しょう} (excerpt, extract) + {録|ろく} (record) → recorded excerpt

VERB FORM:
{抄録|しょうろく}する (to make an abstract, to excerpt)

ACADEMIC USAGE:
{抄録|しょうろく} is essential in academic publishing. It appears at the beginning of papers and helps researchers quickly determine if a paper is relevant to their research.

COMPONENTS OF AN ABSTRACT:
- {目的|もくてき} (purpose)
- {方法|ほうほう} (methods)
- {結果|けっか} (results)
- {結論|けつろん} (conclusion)

RELATED WORDS:
- {要約|ようやく} (summary - more general)
- {概要|がいよう} (overview, outline)
- {要旨|ようし} (gist, main points)
